ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced KYC/CDD screening of all direct and indirect shareholders, directors, and UBOs against OFAC, UN Security Council, and Colombia's UIAF and Procuraduría General lists; PEP status determination is mandatory for all shareholders owning 10% or more; companies in wholesale mineral trading must apply Circular Básica Jurídica No. 005 de 2022 risk-management rules, including transaction monitoring and reporting of suspicious operations to UIAF within one business day.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES – Registro Único Empresarial (www.rues.org.co) via Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá or any local chamber
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All proposed corporate names must be rendered in Spanish or in Latin-script transliteration; foreign-language words are permitted only when they are common industry terms or appear in the statutory objects and are not false or misleading; the name must satisfy the 'single distinct name' rule within the national jurisdiction and cannot be so similar to an existing name that confusion is likely.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a recurso de reposición before the same Cámara de Comercio within 10 business days of notification, setting out arguments of distinctiveness and supporting evidence; if the recurso is denied, a recurso de apelación may be filed before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio within 5 business days; alternatively, the applicant may wait 30 days and file a new homonym clearance request with a modified name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered physical address in Colombia is mandatory under Law 1258 of 2008 and the Commercial Code; for a low-risk wholesale mineral trading company, a virtual administrative office may be used for correspondence and staff logistics, but the statutory registered address must be a physical Colombian location at which the company is accessible to the registry and tax authorities; under no circumstances can the company have only an electronic address as its legal domicile.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk: 3%–5% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Superintendencia de Sociedades or DIAN in the first year of operation; this risk rises moderately if the company registers under ISIC 4669 with high invoice volumes.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (S.A.S. Law), articles 1-5, 17, 20 and 30; applicable registration provisions of the Código de Comercio arts. 110-115; Decree 2249/2015 (RUES), as in force.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) online platform operated jointly with DIAN.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation instrument), optionally elevated to Escritura Pública (Public Deed) at the shareholders' election.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-in capital under Ley 1258 de 2008; capital must be fully subscribed but payment may be deferred up to twenty-four months per the statutory payment schedule. No escrow account requirement; capital may be contributed in cash, assets, or services.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION 2026-001: The founding shareholders of [Company] S.A.S., acting under Ley 1258 of 2008 and the draft by-laws, adopt: (1) Ratification of the incorporation instrument and share subscription schedule; (2) Adoption of the registered office at Calle 100 No. 19-52, Bogotá D.C.; (3) Appointment of the Legal Representative and General Secretary as stated in Annex A; (4) Authorization to open bank accounts, issue SWIFT and letter-of-credit instruments, and engage port agents; (5) Authorization to file the RUT, RUES registrations, and all environment, customs, port and occupational permits; (6) Ratification of founders' prior acts. The Secretary shall certify this resolution upon share-quota-paid-in evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio via RUES online window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two preferred company names through the RUES 'solicitud de autorización de uso de nombre' module; pay the fee electronically via PSE; obtain the name-availability certificate valid for 90 days. Ensure the name does not conflict with existing trademarks or registered entities.
required_dossiers: Name availability request form (Formulario RUES)
Copy of valid ID (cédula or passport) of each founder
If a founder is a legal entity, certificate of existence and representation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises a similarity or trademark objection, file an alternative name list within five business days without additional fee; escalate through the Chamber's administrative review if the objection is deemed erroneous.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Incorporation Instrument and By-Laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría or private signature ceremony under Ley 1258 de 2008
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the by-laws and private incorporation instrument containing corporate purpose, capital schedule, governance rules, and registered office. Have all founders sign and fingerprint the document; if assets are contributed, the founders must execute a public deed or authentic acknowledgment before a notary.
required_dossiers: Draft by-laws and incorporation instrument
Identity documents of founders and official translations if foreign
Capital contribution evidence or payment schedule
Name-availability certificate referenced in the instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notarial objection is raised, correct the by-laws by private deed amendment and re-submit; if statutory form is defective, execute a fresh instrument with curative recitals.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration with the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio with jurisdiction over the registered office (RUES)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed incorporation instrument, name certificate, and registration forms through RUES; pay the registration fee (derechos de inscripción), commercial registry tax, and registration tax. Upon approval, obtain the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal and the company's Matrícula Mercantil.
required_dossiers: Signed incorporation instrument (or public deed)
Name-availability certificate
RUT pre-registration form issued by DIAN
Power of attorney if filed by a representative
Proof of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any Chamber requerimiento within ten business days with clarifications or amended documents; if the application is rejected, correct the defect and re-file without a new name certificate if the original is still valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – Sede Electrónica
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) form through DIAN's virtual office using the Chamber registration data; select tax regime (Impuesto sobre la Renta, IVA if applicable), and obtain the Número de Identificación Tributaria (NIT). For non-resident shareholders, attach sworn beneficial-ownership statements.
required_dossiers: RUT form (electronic)
Certificate of incorporation and legal representation issued by the Chamber
Founders' identification documents
Proof of registered-office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects or queries the application, correct the RUT data in the virtual portal within ten business days; request a DIAN appointment for manual correction in case of systemic error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account and Trade-Finance Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks supervised by Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate checking account and apply for a SWIFT/Letter-of-Credit facility. Submit the legal-existence certificate, NIT, by-laws, and shareholder KYC forms; complete the bank's AML risk assessment (Low_Risk_Standard) and sign the account mandate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of existence and legal representation (less than 30 days old)
Company NIT assignment proof
Institutional by-laws and first board resolution
Beneficial-ownership and PEP declarations for each shareholder
Audited or initial financial statements if available
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the compliance department escalates, provide amended KYC forms and source-of-funds evidence; if the bank rejects the application, apply to an alternative institution and engage the Superintendencia Financiera complaints mechanism for unreasonable delay.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No statutory industrial license applies to pure mineral-ore wholesale brokerage; optional registration with the Agencia Nacional de Minería (ANM) as a mineral trader and, if cross-border operations are conducted, with the Ministerio de Comercio, Industria y Turismo (MinCIT) via the Ventanilla Única de Comercio Exterior (VUCE).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No mandatory operating permit for contract-based brokerage; voluntary Registro de Comercializador de Minerales (ANM) and VUCE import/export permits required only when directly transacting customs movements.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) with local Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) where a physical site is involved
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III – Environmental registration/exemption for pure brokerage without port or warehouse footprint; Full EIA (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental) required only for construction of a sulfur dry-bulk terminal or permanent storage facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If a facility is established, wastewater discharges must comply with Resolución 0631 de 2015; sulfur dust, particulate matter and SO2/H2S emissions in the storage vicinity must comply with Resolución 2254 de 2017 air-quality standards; use covered conveying, wet-suppression and odor-control systems.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate (Certificado de Bomberos) and structural inspection are required for any leased office or warehouse; occupational risk prevention program and workplace-safety clearance must comply with Decreto 1072 de 2015 (Chapter 6) and Resolución 0312 de 2019 regarding emergency response and occupational health.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (National Tax and Customs Directorate); taxpayer portal: Muisca (muisca.dian.gov.co) and DIAN website https://www.dian.gov.co.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (SAS), procure the NIT through: (1) incorporation before the competent Cámara de Comercio; (2) issuance of the legal representative's identity credentials and power of attorney; (3) pre-registration and registration of the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) through DIAN's Muisca portal, selecting NIT, income tax and IVA responsibilities, exporter status, and relevant electronic-invoicing obligations; (4) activation of the DIAN digital certificate required for factura electrónica; and (5) subsequent update of the RUT for changes in economic activities, legal representative, or address. A foreign entity without a permanent establishment may obtain a direct NIT through DIAN by appointing a tax representative in Colombia and validating identity documents; however, a Colombian SAS will normally be the operative tax entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - A Colombian-resident SAS is the taxpayer and is subject to national corporate income tax on worldwide income; shareholders bear a separate dividend tax at distribution. SAS has limited liability. No U.S.-style check-the-box pass-through is permitted. Non-resident entities are taxed on Colombian-source income on a territorial basis.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists in Colombia. A SAS may choose between the ordinary corporate income tax regime and the SIMPLE/Monotributo optional regime if it satisfies the statutory size and gross-revenue thresholds (gross income under 47,000 UVT). Hybrid mismatch treatment is governed by OECD-style anti-hybrid rules enacted under Law 2277 of 2022, which limit deduction or require conformity for hybrid instruments; no elective de-grouping is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA - Impuesto sobre las Ventas (Colombian national value-added tax, VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies for VAT registration: any person performing a taxable act in Colombia or importing goods must register for IVA in the RUT, even with minimal turnover. For the optional SIMPLE/Monotributo regime, the annual gross-income ceiling is 47,000 UVT (2025 UVT approximate value COP 49,799, representing approximately COP 2,340,553,000); normal commercial exporters are not exempt from VAT registration and must register to issue zero-rated export invoices and claim refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: DIAN mandates pre-validation electronic invoicing (factura electrónica de venta) for all taxpayers with invoicing obligations. Invoices must be generated through DIAN-approved software providers or DIAN's free web application, transmitted by DSI/API, and validated before delivery to the customer. Each invoice must include the CUDE/CUE unique code, QR code, and valid XML/PDF formats. Export invoices must be zero-rated and identify the foreign purchaser, Incoterms, and supporting export declaration. Export declarations (DEX) are transmitted electronically through VUCE and DIAN's Muisca platform; real-time digital fiscal clearance is mandatory, with no requirement for physical stamping.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Articles 481 and 489 of the Colombian Tax Code, exports of tangible goods such as granular sulfur mineral ore, and qualifying services supplied to foreign markets or for use abroad, are 'exentos' and effectively taxed at a 0% VAT rate. The SAS must hold a valid RUT with IVA responsibility, transfer title to a foreign purchaser, physically exit Colombian customs territory with a definitive export declaration, and maintain evidence of actual dispatch and payment. The zero-rating confers a right to claim refund or offset of input VAT attributable to the exported operation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DEX (Declaración de Exportación) electronic customs declaration, accepted and validated by DIAN/VUCE
Factura Comercial (commercial invoice with 10-digit HS code, Incoterms, origin, commodity description, and quantity)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or multimodal transport document issued to the exporter and consigned to the foreign buyer
Certificado de Reintegro de Divisas / foreign-exchange surrender certificate or bank confirmation issued through the Colombian foreign exchange market
Certificado de Origen (only when a preferential trade agreement is claimed)
Any contractual documents evidencing the export transaction, price, freight, and payment terms
Ingreso or port customs exit record (registry of final departure)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN will verify the DEX, bill of lading, customs exit records, commercial terms, and the actual foreign-currency surrender through the Colombian foreign exchange market. If export zero-rating is improperly claimed, the VAT export credit or refund is retroactively reversed with default interest calculated from the original refund or offset date. Penalties under Articles 647 and 648 of the Tax Code include the 'inexactitud' fine of up to 160% of the understated tax, plus monetary interest. Misdeclaration may be treated as tax or customs fraud under Decree 1165/2019 and Law 1762/2015, leading to asset forfeiture, cancellation of the exporter registration, customs smuggling charges, and criminal liability for the legal representative. DIAN may open an inspection within the statutory fiscal-investigation period and claw back all zero-rated benefits attributable to the false export.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia) as the controlling authority of the Colombian Foreign Exchange Regime under Decree 1735 of 1993 and the external finance rules and regulations issued by the Board of Directors; the National Tax and Customs Administration (DIAN) supervises foreign trade formalities and import/export documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia maintains a market-oriented foreign exchange regime with full convertibility for current payments and a partially free capital account. Profit remittance through dividends is permitted without prior exchange-control approval once the profits have complied with Colombian taxation; the funds must be routed through an authorized foreign exchange intermediary with the corresponding foreign exchange declaration ('declaración de cambio'). Practical hurdles include the need to evidence the original registration of the inbound foreign investment (if applicable), the presentation of tax payment and withholding certificates for dividend distributions, and the obligation to use an authorized local bank for settlement. Capital injections require prior or simultaneous registration with the Investor Registry maintained by Banco de la República to secure future dividends and capital repatriation rights. There is no blanket currency rationing, but administrative documentation deficiencies can delay repatriation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Colombian foreign exchange regulations compel exporters of goods to collect their foreign currency proceeds within the foreign exchange market through an authorized intermediary. The statutory channeling deadline for export proceeds is generally six months from the date of shipment, with the ability to request extensions for longer-term commercial settlements, particularly in the minerals and commodities sector. The exporter must file, or cause its intermediary to file, an electronic exchange declaration within the required timeframe upon the receipt of funds. There is no fixed percentage of mandatory conversion to Colombian pesos; instead, the entire commercial amount of export proceeds must be repatriated and made available inside the Colombian banking system, either in COP or in authorized foreign-currency accounts, and must be supported by export invoices, bills of lading and customs clearance records as required by Banco de la República and DIAN.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with Commercial and Foreign Trade Desk / Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account with Export Collections and Letter of Credit Desk / Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Foreign Exchange Settlement Account / Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account with Forex Lines and International Trade Services / Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Trade Finance Account / Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low legal viability as a standalone clearing rail for the Colombian sas entity. Offshore electronic money institutions and fintech EMIs are not recognized as authorized foreign exchange intermediaries in Colombia; they cannot receive Colombian export proceeds, issue valid exchange declarations, or legally clear COP trade transactions. They have a medium complementary role for invoicing or collecting funds in third-country currencies that do not enter Colombia and do not affect the local foreign exchange obligation, but all permissible FX-regulated flows must settle through a licensed Colombian commercial bank or authorized financial corporation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A fully remote account opening is not uniformly accepted. In practice, Colombian tier-one banks require the legal representative, and often all natural-person shareholders holding a qualifying percentage, to complete a live KYC interview; this interview may be conducted through a secure video call combined with digital signature and biometric verification, but several banks mandate the initial physical appearance of at least one director or attorney-in-fact at the client service office. Non-resident directors without an active Colombian visa or local presence must have their identity, signature and corporate powers verified through a notary abroad, apostilled and translated into Spanish, and some banks require a local legal representative with a Colombian power of attorney to handle account mandates and banking proceedings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in the ultimate beneficial ownership structure, particularly involving non-resident shareholders in non-cooperative jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate chain to the ultimate natural persons; apostilled certificates of incorporation and in-force good standing certificates; passport copies and proof of residential address; corporate and shareholder resolutions authorizing the account; sworn declarations of source of wealth and source of trade funds; tax identification evidence for each structuring entity; and a written legal memorandum from Colombian counsel explaining the ownership map and the business rationale for the Colombian SAS.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient operational history or absence of audited financial statements for a newly established mineral-ore trading entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) audited balance sheet and profit-and-loss statement, if available; interim management accounts; bank references from the parent company; executed purchase and sale agreements for granular sulfur cargo; supplier invoices and end-customer purchase orders; vessel nomination and charter party summaries; cargo surveyor and inspection certificates; and proof of a committed working capital credit facility or parent-company undertaking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential PEP or sanctions-list screening hits on counterparties, directors or the routing jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence report from a reputable compliance analytics provider; negative media and Politically Exposed Persons screening results; explanations for any exact or close-name matches; a legal opinion from Colombian counsel confirming the absence of mandatory disqualification; source of trade funds and source of third-party wealth documentation; and a rectification letter demonstrating that the PEP/sanction alert does not correspond to the beneficial owner or to any transacting party.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Characterization of granular sulfur as a potentially restricted or dual-use industrial chemical.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: International Material Safety Data Sheet; product specification sheet from the final refinery or receiving manufacturer; isolated purity test certificate for the consignment; end-user certificate from the overseas customer; final destination port and unloading contract; an export control self-assessment prepared by Colombian counsel under Decree 519/2000 and related regulations; and a written statement confirming that ISIC 4669 wholesale trading does not include controlled arms, military materials, or chemical weapons precursors.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity contributions from the foreign parent must be routed by SWIFT MT103 wire from the parent bank account to the SAS bank account at a Colombian authorized commercial bank. The wire should include a clear beneficiary NIT (Colombian tax ID) of the SAS, the bank account number, and a remittance purpose text such as 'Capital contribution / Foreign direct investment into CO_SAS' with the foreign exchange concept indicated as an inbound capital injection. The receiving local bank will require the company to evidence the corporate resolution authorizing the increase or creation of equity and, where necessary, prepare the registration with the Banco de la República's International Investments Registry to secure subsequent repatriation rights. The bank will draft and file the required 'declaración de cambio' and will assign the funds to a standard operational account or a capital escrow account until final disbursement in accordance with the corporate purpose. All funds must remain traceable through the bank's system, and any subsequent use in trade-related expenses should be documented against invoices, voyage orders, commodity contracts and purchase orders.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade settlements under open account terms, the clearing rail is a SWIFT MT103 payment, initiated through an authorized Colombian bank's international wire desk with a detailed 70-field reference stating the invoice number, purchase order, port of loading, bill of lading number and cargo description. For documentary trade, the standard rail is a commercial letter of credit issued by the client's foreign bank, advised or confirmed through a Colombian bank using SWIFT MT700/MT702; amendments and collaterals use MT707 and MT760 formats. Payment against a complying presentation will be released through the Colombian bank's correspondent network as a reimbursement MT202 or a direct MT103. All outbound disbursements must be accompanied by VAT, withholding tax and foreign exchange declaration forms, and should be mapped in the corporate ERP to the underlying commercial trade document to satisfy banking audit and AML requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable US Dollar to Colombian Peso forward contract executed with an authorized Colombian commercial bank
Cross-currency swap between USD and COP used for matching trade receivables and payables
Vanilla US Dollar to Colombian Peso options, including calls and puts, executed with a licensed financial intermediary

NDF (non-deliverable forward) contracted offshore or onshore only when the transaction has a verifiable underlying trade exposure and is carried out under Banco de la República's derivative-market authorization

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% flat rate for FY2024 and subsequent years (Art. 240 E.T.); large extractive enterprises with net income above 880,000 UVT (approx. COP 41.4 billion in 2024) incur an additional 5% surtax on solid-mineral extraction income, and 10% for oil/coal extraction; a pure trading/brokerage vehicle is generally outside this surtax unless the group operates extractive mines.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sectoral tax holiday for commodity trading; available incentives: 20% CIT for Free Trade Zone companies; 0% CIT participation exemption on dividends received from qualifying Colombian or foreign subsidiaries; unlimited NOL carryforward capped annually at 25% of ordinary net income; potential 0% WHT on qualifying dividends under the Colombian Holding Company (CHC) regime; export sales are VAT-exempt (0%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carryforward), with the annual compensation cap of 25% of ordinary net taxable income of the year (Art. 147 E.T.); losses must be adjusted for inflation and cannot be carried to offset presumptive income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 'Declaración de Renta y Complementario de Personas Jurídicas y Asimiladas' filed through the DIAN electronic system (MUISCA / SIRE at www.dian.gov.co) using a digital certificate; a sworn public-accountant certification is mandatory for taxpayers with gross income above 200,000 UVT.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a 31-December year-end, the CIT return is due between 22 August and 10 September of the following year, assigned by the last two digits of the NIT (DIAN Resolution each year); the tax is paid in two equal instalments (50% at filing and 50% before December of the same year), plus the advance CIT payment ('anticipo') of up to 100% of the prior year's liability for large taxpayers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Heading codes (NIT, DV, fiscal year, CIIU 4669)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification, taxable period, economic-activity code (CIIU 4669 wholesale of mineral ores) and form version.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Colombian NIT of the S.A.S.; the legal representative (who may be a foreign-resident individual) must be duly registered in the authentic registry, and the foreign parent's corporate details go in the annex, not the heading.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from sulfur ore trading, brokerage commissions, demurrage recovery and freight forwarding charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Colombian-source and foreign-source income earned by the resident entity; income from international sale of goods is taxable in full, with no territorial exclusion; foreign-currency LC proceeds are translated at the DIAN exchange rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutorily excluded income, such as VAT collected, capital reimbursements and qualifying dividends received.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends from non-resident subsidiaries qualify for the participation exemption only if the CHC/Art. 242 E.T. tests are met; otherwise they are taxable; maintain ownership and substance evidence in the TP/ESR file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Renglon 80 'Costos de la venta de bienes'
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold for the sulfur ore, including FOB purchase price, marine freight, insurance, handling and port costs capitalizable in the inventory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support each purchase with commercial invoice, bill of lading, LC documentation and customs DEX entries; resale title transfer must be evidenced; otherwise DIAN may reclassify the operation as pure brokerage commissions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary business expenses: ocean freight, port charges, agency fees, demurrage, legal/audit costs, salaries, interest and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions require causal link to Colombian-source income; related-party interest is capped by the 3:1 thin-capitalization rule; foreign invoices must be translated and form part of the transfer pricing file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income (rare for trading) and the resulting net taxable income before NOL compensation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim exemptions without an advance tax ruling; for non-resident controlled traders, almost all brokerage income is taxable; apply the NOL cap of 25% in Renglon 108.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The tax generated at 35% (Gravamen a los Ingresos, adjustments, losses, credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No deduction is allowed for dividends distributed to the foreign parent; the sobretasa situation is assessed only if the group is an extractive producer; foreign tax credits are limited to the Colombian tax on the same income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annex 'Dividendos pagados a accionistas del exterior' (Art. 245 E.T.)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of dividends declared and the corresponding WHT to be paid to DIAN; not part of the main income tax computation but filed with it.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 10% WHT on the portion previously taxed at the corporate level and 35% on the untaxed portion; if a tax treaty applies, compute the reduced rate and attach the TRC and beneficial-ownership evidence before the payment date.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: surcharge of 5% per month or fraction on the tax due, up to 100% of the tax (minimum COP 470,650 equal to 10 UVT in 2024); if no tax is due, 1% per month on gross income or assets. Inaccuracy/omission: penalty of 160% of the omitted tax. Late payment: default interest at the certified DIAN rate (approx. 2.7% monthly / 32.4% annual in 2024) plus automatic collection and attachment orders.
